scope: Exactly six completed Matrix/RandomMatrix atlas cards and their required proof dependencies.

hypotheses: $X$ is real symmetric, $X_{ij}=b_{ij}g_{ij}$ for $i\ge j$, with independent standard real Gaussians and symmetric $b_{ij}\ge0$.
records.readback: The genuine symmetric independent lower-triangular Gaussian construction satisfies the two-sided unnormalized Schatten moment estimate for every real p>=2. The row-square-sum and row-maximum profiles match the card, with dimension/profile/exponent independent constants 1/100 and 512. Zero profiles and empty dimensions are covered; no moment bound is assumed.

hypotheses: $X$ is real symmetric, $X_{ij}=b_{ij}g_{ij}$ for $i\ge j$, with independent standard real Gaussians and symmetric $b_{ij}\ge0$.
records.conclusion: There is universal $C\ge1$ with $\mathbb P\{R_p(X)\ge t\}\le\mathbb P\{\|X\|_{S_p}\ge t\}\le C\mathbb P\{R_p(X)\ge t/C\}$ for $t\ge0$. In particular $\mathbb E R_p(X)\le\mathbb E\|X\|_{S_p}\le C\mathbb E R_p(X)$.
records.readback: The same genuine Gaussian construction satisfies both expectation inequalities and both upper-tail comparisons, for every t>=0 and every native extended exponent p>=2, including infinity. One explicit constant independent of profile, dimension and exponent serves both conclusions. No upper expectation comparison is assumed.

records.conclusion: If $\operatorname{ds}(T)\le\varepsilon\le1/(n+1)$, then $\operatorname{rank}T(X)\ge\operatorname{rank}X$ for every $X\succeq0$ and $(1-\sqrt{n\varepsilon})^n\le\operatorname{cap}(T)\le1$. Conversely, $\operatorname{cap}(T)\ge e^{-\delta}$, $0\le\delta\le1/6$, implies $\operatorname{ds}(T)\le6\delta$.
records.readback: Under either T(I)=I or T*(I)=I, the remaining Frobenius-square defect equals ds(T). The original epsilon<=1/(n+1) range gives rank nondecrease for every PSD input and (1-sqrt(n*epsilon))^n<=cap(T)<=1. Both normalized converses give ds(T)<=6*delta on 0<=delta<=1/6. Four reviewed clauses cover both branches.

clauses.statement: For each normalization T(I)=I or T*(I)=I, squared normalization defect at most epsilon <= 1/(n+1) implies rank(T(X)) >= rank(X) for every PSD input X. The normalized defect is the remaining Frobenius-square term.
For each normalization the exact lower capacity bound is (1-sqrt(n*epsilon))^n, with the same epsilon range and without capacity attainment.
For positive matrix dimension, either normalization gives cap(T) <= 1.
Under either normalization, cap(T) >= exp(-delta), 0 <= delta <= 1/6, bounds the sum of the two Frobenius-square defects by 6*delta.

sources.label: Definition 2.6, Proposition 2.7, Theorem 3.11, PDF pp. 20 and 33

records.readback: Invertible left/right congruence gives the exact squared determinant factors. Tensor-product capacity has the original dimension exponents, including either factor of zero capacity. Infimum arguments do not assume an attaining minimizer. The two reviewed clauses cover the entire original card.

clauses.statement: Exact invertible congruence scaling of the determinant-one capacity, including zero capacity and without an attaining minimizer.
Tensor-product capacity equals cap(T1)^n2 cap(T2)^n1 for all positive finite dimensions and all finite Kraus families, including either factor of zero capacity.

hypotheses: $A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$, $1\le k<\operatorname{rank}A$; $\sigma_i(A)$ are decreasing and zero-padded, with one-based indices.
records.conclusion: There is a universal $C>0$ and $\sigma\subseteq[m]$, $|\sigma|=k$, such that $AJ_\sigma$ is injective and $\|(AJ_\sigma)^{-1}:A(\mathbb R^\sigma)\to\mathbb R^\sigma\|_2\le C\min_{k<r\le\operatorname{rank}A}\sqrt{\frac{mr}{(r-k)\sum_{i=r}^m\sigma_i(A)^2}}$.
records.readback: For every 1<=k<rank(A), an exact k-column subset is injective and its actual Euclidean inverse on its range satisfies the literal finite-minimum bound with universal C=2. The index set is Icc(k+1,rank(A)), including the rank endpoint. The zero-based tail at r-1 is the one-based source tail starting at r. A stronger simultaneous all-r statement is also exported.

records.conclusion: Some $\sigma\subseteq[m]$ has $|\sigma|\ge\lfloor\varepsilon^2\|L\|_F^2/\|L\|_2^2\rfloor$, independent columns $(Lv_i)_{i\in\sigma}$, and $\|\sum_{i\in\sigma}a_iLv_i\|_2^2>(1-\varepsilon)^2\|L\|_F^2\|a\|_2^2/m$ for every nonzero $a\in\mathbb R^\sigma$.
records.readback: An actual isotropic finite frame and arbitrary nonzero real square L give a subset of exactly floor(epsilon^2*frobSq(L)/specNorm(L)^2) indices. The selected transformed columns are linearly independent. Every nonzero Euclidean coefficient vector satisfies the strict original (1-epsilon)^2 bound, including the vacuous empty selection case.
